fields.Front: Case study: what are the attributes of DEPARTMENT, and which are keys?
fields.Back: Name (key), Number (key), Locations (multi-valued). Also the manager and start date come via the MANAGES relationship.

fields.Front: Case study: what are the attributes of EMPLOYEE?
fields.Back: Name, SSN (key), Address, Salary, Sex, Birthdate.

fields.Front: Case study: what are the attributes of PROJECT?
Case study: what are the attributes of DEPENDENT?
fields.Back: Name, Sex, Birthdate, Relationship (relation to the employee).

fields.Text: In the case study the multi-valued attribute is Department {{c1::Locations}} ('a department may have several locations').

fields.Front: Case study: list the relationships with their cardinality ratios.
fields.Back: MANAGES (Employee 1:1 Department, attribute StartDate); WORKS FOR (Employee N:1 Department); CONTROLS (Department 1:N Project); WORKS ON (Employee M:N Project, attribute Hours); SUPERVISES (Employee 1:N Employee, unary); DEPENDENTS OF (Employee 1:N Dependent, identifying).

fields.Front: Case study: which relationship carries the attribute Hours, and why is it not on EMPLOYEE or PROJECT?
fields.Back: WORKS ON; hours depend on the (employee, project) pair, not on either entity alone.

fields.Text: In the case study, StartDate is an attribute of the {{c1::MANAGES}} relationship.
The case study's unary (recursive) relationship is {{c1::SUPERVISES}} (Employee to Employee).

fields.Front: Case study: which entity is weak, who is its owner, and what is its partial key?
fields.Back: DEPENDENT; owner EMPLOYEE; partial key Name (via identifying relationship DEPENDENTS OF).

fields.Front: Case study: participation of EMPLOYEE and DEPARTMENT in WORKS FOR?
fields.Back: Both total: every employee works for a department (1,1) and every department has employees (1,N).

fields.Front: Case study: participation of EMPLOYEE and DEPARTMENT in MANAGES?
fields.Back: EMPLOYEE partial (0,1): not every employee manages. DEPARTMENT total (1,1): every department has a manager.
